description:
Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

GET TO KNOW US

At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we’re on a mission to make every company a wellness company.We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you’ll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally. 

Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are hiring a Sales Development Senior Manager to join our Sales team in Berlin! 

This is a hybrid role, requiring a minimum of two days per week in our office.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Act as the direct leader and mentor for our front-line Business Development Representative (BDR) team, fostering a culture of growth and purpose.
  • Conduct live call-shadowing and deep-dive reviews to sharpen your team's ability to communicate the transformative power of Wellhub.
  • Take full accountability for a team of 5–8 BDRs, guiding their professional journey and ensuring they hit the milestones that drive our mission forward.
  • Lead the interview process for new talent and execute a seamless onboarding program that gets new starters hitting "active" status within 30 days.
  • Excellence in building strong partnerships with marketing and sales.
  • Deeply understand the UK B2B ecosystem to teach your team how to position wellbeing as a "business-critical" priority for CHROs and CFOs.
  • Pivot messaging based on market shifts to ensure Wellhub remains a vital solution for companies navigating industry headwinds.
  • Manage the "speed-to-lead" for inbound inquiries, ensuring high conversion rates through rigorous qualification.
  • Work with the team to build hyper-personalised outbound "clusters." You’ll move beyond generic sequences to high-intent, research-backed prospecting.
  • Ensure the team is getting maximum ROI out of Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and AI-assisted prospecting tools.
  • Develop the best-in-class strategies for managing the rep's book of business and running the outreach-prospecting playbook and turning curiosity into attention with intention.
  • Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life wellness.

WHO YOU ARE

  • Proven Track Record: 5+ years in Sales, with at least 1-2 years of experience as a Lead BDR or Front-line Manager.
  • The "Coach" DNA: A passion for seeing others succeed.
  • You can look at a conversion funnel and pinpoint exactly where the "leak" is-whether it’s the initial hook, the discovery call, or the hand-off to the AE.
  • Proven experience managing SDR/BDR teams for a Challenger Brand or a "non-commodity" solution.
  • You must demonstrate the ability to create urgency for a product that is not yet a "household name" or is perceived as discretionary spend.
  • You have moved beyond "feature-selling" and can coach reps to pivot from Product Interest to Business Impact.
  • You should be able to show how you’ve successfully positioned a solution as "mission-critical" during budget-conscious cycles.
  • You are familiar with the HR space and can talk the CHRO language.

We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. 

 

WHAT WE OFFER YOU 

With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life. Our benefits include:

WELLHUB:  Free Gold membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you. 

FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role is Hybrid, with a minimum of 2 days per week in-office. We offer all employees a one-time reimbursement to set up their home office equipment and a monthly work allowance to help cover the costs of working from home.

FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE:  Flexibility for us isn’t just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

PAID TIME OFF: We know how important it is to take time away from work to recharge. Employees receive a minimum of 25 days paid holiday per year (including an extra holiday on your birthday!).

PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. We offer 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. Parents giving birth are eligible for an extended leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while they get settled.  

CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions,  build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success. 

CULTURE: You’ll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here. 

And to get a glimpse of life at Wellhub… Follow us on Instagram @lifeatwellhub and LinkedIn!

 

Diversity, Equity, and Belonging at Wellhub

Augustus collapses this stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code. description: SAEKI - Manufacturing at software speed Europe's defense industrial base cannot respond at the speed modern conflict requires. Legacy suppliers operate on month-long timelines. Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile. SAEKI is building the operating system for autonomous factories - the infrastructure that lets Europe manufacture mission-critical components at software speed. The Role As a Computational Geometry Engineer, you own the geometry core of our Manufacturing Intelligence stack - the engine that takes an arbitrary customer CAD model and reasons about how to build it, and then proves that we built it right. You own the code that runs in the factory. What We're Looking For 5+ years building geometry-heavy software in production - CAD/CAM, geometry kernels, feature recognition, CAE/simulation preparation, metrology, or comparable. B-rep and Mesh Depth. You think natively in topology and NURBS. Feature recognition, defeaturing, robust booleans, offsetting, surface/surface intersection, healing and repair. You know exactly why floating-point robustness destroys naive implementations - and what to do about it. You have had the opportunity to delve into complex CAD models and are able to assess their quality in both quantitative and qualitative terms (gaps in edge, spikes in loops, tiny elements, twisted surfaces...) and ultimately predict which types of processing might be challenged. Kernel Fluency. Hands-on with a geometry kernel - Parasolid, OpenCASCADE, ACIS, or equivalent - and the judgment to know which parts can be developed in-house in order to retain full control and IP rights, and which parts too complex (e.g. advanced solvers) should be integrated as 3rd parties. Comfortable with mesh and point-cloud processing (libigl, Open3D, CGAL, PCL) alongside solid modelling.You know well STEP file format and about integration into collaboration & interoperability processes. Technical Excellence. Strong command of modern C++ (17+), plus Python for rapid iteration. Rust is welcome. You write and test performant code. Manufacturing Instinct. Some knowledge of fabrication techniques-casting, stamping, composites, and additive manufacturing-alongside toolsets for evaluating design manufacturability, risk profiles, quality standards, and cost factors. End-to-End Ownership. Algorithm design through to a shipped, tested, maintained service. First Principles Thinker. You reason by physics and mathematics, not analogy. When an algorithm fails on a real part, you know whether the bug is in the code, the model, or the assumption. Industrial Grit. You want to stand next to the machine in Germany and watch your output run. The feedback loop between your code and cutting metal is the point. Maniacal Urgency. Speed is our only edge. You thrive in the "chaos-to-order" phase of a startup. On-site: Ability to work in person at our HQ in Zurich, Switzerland. What we're not looking for Researchers who want to publish and hand off. You ship. CAD users. This is a role for people who build the tools, not drive them. Engineers who need a clean spec. The problem is defined by the part, the machine, and the customer - you'll go find it. People who treat "it works on the test model" as done. Real customer CAD is broken, degenerate, and adversarial. That is the job. Engineers who are uncomfortable with ambiguity or rapidly changing priorities. What we offer Mission: Rebuild the industrial sovereignty of the West. Your work directly enables production of mission-critical hardware for defense and space. Total Ownership: High-stakes autonomy in your domain. You own both the problems and the solutions - and have the authority to execute. The Environment: Access to a 8,000 m² state-of-the-art facility featuring 5-axis CNCs, industrial robots, and industrial 3D printers. Your algorithms run on real hardware from day one. The Team: "Special Forces" model. Everyone senior, everyone ships. No politics, no bureaucracy. Direct feedback, high standards. Compensation: Competitive salary + meaningful equity. Location: Zurich HQ, with occasional time at Factory ONE in Munich. Apply Resume: Focus on geometry systems you've built and owned. GitHub/Portfolio: Show us the hard problem you solved - code, papers, or parts that came off a machine because of you. Cover letter: Why this mission? Why now? What would you build first? IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Location: This role is based onsite in Geneva, Switzerland.
Travel: 
Job ID: 1893 

ID Quantique (IDQ), part of IonQ, is a global leader in quantum-safe communications. We provide solutions to protect governments, telecommunication infrastructures, and banking & financial institutions from the “harvest-now, decrypt-later” threat, delivering both terrestrial and space-based quantum-safe networks in live operation globally.

The Role: 

We are looking for a Staff Cryptography Engineer to join our team building post-quantum cryptography (PQC) hardware acceleration for HSM and network-appliance products. You will implement the software side of modern post-quantum algorithms: reference models, optimised implementations, and the test infrastructure that proves they are correct. This is a hands-on development role at the heart of applied cryptography, working with some of the most experienced cryptographic engineers in the field.

Responsibilities:

You will implement and maintain reference and bit-accurate models of ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA/LMS in C/C++/Rust and Python, develop constant-time software implementations of cryptographic functions, and build out the known-answer-test and test-vector tooling (NIST ACVP) used for verification and CAVP certification. You will contribute to the decomposition of algorithms into hardware-friendly building blocks (Keccak, NTT and polynomial arithmetic, samplers, encode/decode), support RTL and firmware engineers with algorithm questions and debugging, and help evaluate third-party cryptographic libraries, working under the guidance of our senior cryptography engineers.

  • Implement reference models, optimised software and test-vector infrastructure for ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA/LMS
  • Support hardware and firmware teams with algorithm expertise, debugging and certification-oriented tooling

Requirements:

We are looking for a candidate with a Master’s degree (PhD a plus) in Cryptography, Mathematics, Computer Science or a related field and at least five years of experience implementing cryptographic algorithms or security-critical software in C/C++ or Rust. You have solid understanding of modern cryptographic primitives and ideally first exposure to post-quantum schemes (lattice-based or hash-based) and their underlying mathematics.

You care about correctness and write well-tested, readable code; you understand what constant-time implementation means and why it matters. Familiarity with NIST test-vector formats, CAVP/ACVP or certification-oriented development is a plus. Fluency in English is required; French or German is an advantage.

  • Hands-on developer of cryptographic or security-critical software with strong C/C++/Rust skills
  • Solid cryptographic foundations with the ambition to build deep post-quantum expertise

Preferred Qualifications:

You want to grow into a world-class applied cryptographer by working on real products with demanding correctness and security requirements, and you enjoy the discipline of code that must be provably right.

  • Flexible work models that let you balance your life, your family, and your career

  • A career development plan within the IonQ group’s companies
  • A dynamic, close-knit environment where you collaborate with a global team of experts

I joined four years ago as a Curriculum Developer and have spent the last couple of years growing Client Education into the (soon to be) five-person team it is today. Before hx I spent a decade teaching Computing in secondary schools. Outside of work most of my time goes to my two children, and what's left to running and, more recently, mountain biking - where I'm still very much a beginner. Client Education exists to get our customers to value as quickly as possible, and to keep them there. We run instructor-led training, own hx Academy where all our self-paced learning content lives, own the certification programme, and run some of our customer events. We've also recently taken ownership of Developer+, and that's where this role comes in. Our first customers are working through the programme now, and as it grows it will need to evolve based on what we learn from them. This isn't a typical Delivery Engineer role, you'll sit in Client Education rather than Delivery Engineering. You'll still work closely with the wider Delivery Engineering team, but your day to day is the customers on Developer+: delivering workshops, running drop-ins, reviewing their code, and shaping the programme around what you learn doing it. You'll partner with Product too, so customers can adopt new enhancements quickly and smoothly. There's no established playbook for this yet, so what matters most is the drive to build one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to own, I'd love to hear from you. About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry: which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes — whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision — helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally — already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do — from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. About the Delivery Engineering team The hyperexponential Delivery Engineering team is a unique blend of engineers, actuaries, mathematicians and data scientists. We don’t take on traditional “transformations” (we have brilliant partners for that) – we specialise in handling only the most difficult and interesting problems our customers face, where only a combination of technical depth, market expertise and hx knowledge will do. The Delivery Engineering team are the experts' experts of the hx platform, knowing it top-to-bottom, inside-out – both breadth and depth. You’ll learn its limits and which can be pushed. You’ll uncover every trick in the book, the secret combinations, and the shortcuts. You’ll combine all of this with a growing knowledge of insurance technology to present 'the art of the possible' to our customers and help shape cutting-edge tech, while working alongside some of the brightest, most ambitious people in the tech and insurance industries. What you'll be doing Move customer teams from hx-led build to independent delivery, shifting effort from pairing toward review and advisory. Keep every engagement moving to its prescribed path, sequencing services to each customer's build stage. Deliver structured enablement sessions — architecture, coding best practice, testing and deployment, model lifecycles — pitched at each team's level. Run code review as a consistent, standards-anchored service, evolving hx's model development standards where reviews expose gaps. Provide drop-in support shaped by each customer's build stage, resolving most issues in session rather than escalating. Make Developer+ repeatable rather than personality-dependent, documenting delivery and using AI to scale capacity. Convert delivery knowledge into hx Academy content, prioritised by what reviews and drop-ins actually surface. Act as the technical voice of the customer into Product, feeding back recurring friction on a regular rhythm. What you'll need to have done Built deep hx platform expertise and production-grade Python, including testing, deployment and model lifecycles. Have excellent pricing and modelling judgement when working with customer’s - working with insurance & actuarial teams is a plus. Developed strong technical enablement instincts, pitching sessions and documentation at the audience's real level. Coached customer teams to work independently rather than solving problems for them. Operated with high ownership and self-direction, building repeatable process where none exists. Prioritised transparently across competing delivery, review and content demands. Communicated with credibility and clarity across developers, actuaries, delivery partners and internal stakeholders. You're unlikely to thrive here if You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach. You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges. You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn't obvious. If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us. Compensation At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make. Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this. Benefits £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development. 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total). Company pension scheme via Penfold. Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life. Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno. Private healthcare insurance through AXA. Income protection and Life Insurance. Cycle to Work Scheme. Additional perks Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.). Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights. Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry. Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together. Interview process Initial call with our Talent team Take-home Python challenge followed by Skills Interview Manager Interview Values Interview Meet the CEO Our commitment to Diversity hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive. Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure. If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team. Next steps If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome. For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page. description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.
 
We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer.

 

About the Role

The Senior Director, Enterprise Business Development – EMEA will report to the Vice President and Managing Director, EMEA and lead the strategy and execution model for CoreWeave’s Enterprise business across the region.

This is a business development and strategy leadership role that works through CoreWeave’s field organisation. Country sales teams will retain account ownership, opportunity management and revenue responsibility, while you define the Enterprise strategy, customer propositions, industry points of view, sales plays and adoption mechanisms that enable them to win and grow strategic Enterprise customers.

You will work closely with Field Sales, Product, Field Engineering, Product and Field Marketing, partners and customers to build a differentiated Enterprise narrative and translate it into repeatable field execution. You will also build and lead a team of Enterprise Business Development Managers aligned to priority vertical industries, bringing deep expertise in how AI will reshape those sectors.

In This Role, You Will

  • Define and execute CoreWeave’s EMEA Enterprise business development strategy in partnership with regional and country sales leadership.
  • Establish CoreWeave’s Enterprise point of view, including Enterprise architecture, market segmentation, AI wallet distribution, buying centres, workload evolution and competitive positioning.
  • Define how CoreWeave participates in the Enterprise AI transformation journey, from initial AI initiatives through production adoption, operationalisation and scaled Enterprise Intelligence.
  • Develop the narrative for how CoreWeave enables customers to operate their AI Learning Loops, positioning the platform as the infrastructure, software and operational foundation through which organisations continuously build, deploy, learn and improve.
  • Build a systematic view of Enterprise AI adoption across EMEA, including where investment is occurring, which workloads are moving into production, how budgets are shifting and where CoreWeave can gain market share.
  • Define Enterprise segmentation and prioritisation models that help field teams identify the customers, industries, workloads and buying centres with the greatest strategic and commercial potential.
  • Develop CoreWeave’s Enterprise sales plays, including target customer profiles, business triggers, technical use cases, executive value propositions, competitive positioning and expansion motions.
  • Own the development of Enterprise sales content, executive narratives, pitch decks and field assets in partnership with Field and Product Marketing.
  • Build a repeatable Enterprise adoption methodology that helps customers progress from initial workload evaluation through production deployment, scaled consumption and broader platform adoption.
  • Develop programmes that enable customers to adopt CoreWeave as a strategic component of their AI architecture rather than as a point solution for individual workloads.
  • Partner with Product leadership to ensure CoreWeave’s Enterprise strategy reflects product capabilities, roadmap direction and the requirements of large-scale Enterprise customers.
  • Translate customer and market insight into clear recommendations for product investment, developer experience, security, governance, observability, integration and Enterprise platform capabilities.
  • Work closely with Field Engineering to define Enterprise adoption strategies using Forward Deployed Engineers, specialist technical resources and services.
  • Build repeatable engagement models that combine business, technical and operational resources around the most important Enterprise transformation opportunities.
  • Partner with Field Sales leaders to translate Enterprise strategy into country and account-level execution, ensuring sellers understand where to focus, what to lead with and how to progress customers through the adoption journey.
  • Work with partners to build joint Enterprise propositions, solution patterns and routes to market that accelerate customer adoption and extend CoreWeave’s reach.
  • Maintain executive-level relationships with strategic Enterprise customers, technology partners and ecosystem leaders.
  • Act as an executive sponsor for strategically important Enterprise transformation opportunities.
  • Build and maintain an active graph of Enterprise AI adoption across the region, mapping customers, industries, workloads, AI investment, architecture choices, partners, competitors and stages of maturity.
  • Build, lead and develop a team of Enterprise Business Development Managers aligned to priority industry segments.
  • Ensure each industry leader develops a differentiated view of how AI will reshape their sector, including priority use cases, economic impact, data and infrastructure requirements, buying centres, barriers to adoption and relevant ecosystem partners.
  • Establish a rigorous operating cadence and scorecard covering market penetration, Enterprise adoption, field execution, pipeline influence, consumption, revenue performance and market share.
  • Represent CoreWeave’s Enterprise narrative externally with customers, partners, industry bodies, analysts, media and at major industry events.

Objectives

During the first 12 months, you will:

  • Define CoreWeave’s EMEA Enterprise strategy, operating plan and growth priorities.
  • Establish a clear Enterprise segmentation model covering priority industries, customers, workloads and buying centres.
  • Develop CoreWeave’s Enterprise architecture and AI transformation points of view.
  • Define the Enterprise AI Learning Loop narrative and articulate how CoreWeave becomes the ways and means through which customers operate and scale those loops.
  • Build the initial Enterprise sales plays, executive narratives, sales content and pitch materials required by field teams.
  • Develop and launch a repeatable Enterprise adoption methodology covering evaluation, production deployment, expansion and scaled adoption.
  • Define the engagement model for Forward Deployed Engineers, Field Engineering and services within strategic Enterprise opportunities.
  • Build and maintain the first regional Enterprise AI adoption graph, identifying market penetration, wallet distribution, major workloads, competitive positions and whitespace.
  • Establish the vertical industry strategy and determine the first priority industry segments.
  • Hire and onboard the initial Enterprise Business Development Managers aligned to those industries.
  • Build executive relationships with an initial set of strategic Enterprise customers and partners.
  • Establish the business review cadence, measurement framework and market-share methodology for the Enterprise segment.
  • Demonstrate measurable contribution to Enterprise pipeline, adoption, consumption and overall EMEA Enterprise revenue performance.

Who You Are

  • 15+ years of experience in enterprise business development, go-to-market strategy, sales, industry leadership, consulting or product strategy within cloud infrastructure, enterprise technology, AI or another complex technology environment.
  • Significant experience defining and executing Enterprise growth strategies across multiple markets or industries.
  • A proven record of translating market and customer insight into repeatable sales plays, adoption programmes and measurable commercial outcomes.
  • Deep understanding of how large Enterprises evaluate, adopt, govern and scale new technology platforms.
  • Strong understanding of Enterprise architecture, cloud infrastructure, AI platforms, data environments and the operational requirements of production AI.
  • Experience developing segmentation models, executive value propositions, sales plays, industry narratives and adoption methodologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to connect technical architecture with business strategy, operating-model change and executive priorities.
  • Experience working closely with field sales organisations to improve customer targeting, opportunity development, competitive positioning and expansion.
  • Experience partnering with Product and Engineering teams to translate Enterprise requirements into roadmap and investment priorities.
  • Experience designing or leading complex customer adoption programmes involving specialist engineering, consulting, services or Forward Deployed teams.
  • Strong understanding of the Enterprise AI buying landscape, including technology budgets, buying centres, strategic partners and evolving workload economics.
  • Demonstrated experience building senior relationships with CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, business leaders and other Enterprise executives.
  • Experience developing industry-specific strategies or leading business development across major Enterprise verticals.
  • Strong analytical capability, with the ability to build market models, adoption frameworks, segmentation strategies and executive-level business reviews.
  • Experience building, hiring, coaching and developing high-performing business development, strategy or industry teams.
  • Proven ability to lead through influence across Sales, Product, Engineering, Marketing and partner organisations.
  • A record of operating successfully across EMEA markets and cultures, with the ability to travel regularly.

Preferred

  • Leadership experience in Enterprise strategy, business development, industry go-to-market or sales at a major hyperscale cloud provider, AI platform company or global infrastructure technology business.
  • Direct experience building or scaling an Enterprise cloud or AI business measured through customer adoption, consumption, revenue and market share.
  • Experience defining Enterprise architecture or transformation points of view used by large customer-facing organisations.
  • Experience building AI, cloud or data-platform adoption methodologies for large Enterprise customers.
  • Experience with Forward Deployed Engineering, professional services, transformation consulting or other high-touch Enterprise adoption models.
  • Deep expertise in one or more major Enterprise industries and a strong understanding of how AI will change industry value chains, operating models and economics.
  • Experience developing public-facing thought leadership and representing a technology company with customers, analysts, media and at major industry events.
  • Established executive relationships across the EMEA Enterprise and technology ecosystem.
  • A bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

Wondering If You’re a Good Fit?

We believe in investing in our people and value candidates who bring different experiences, even if they do not meet every requirement.

  • You are a builder. You are comfortable starting with an ambition, creating the model and then driving it into execution.
  • You can turn a complex technology and market landscape into a clear point of view that customers and field teams can act on.
  • You can move comfortably between a CIO, a product leader, a field seller, an engineer and an industry executive.
  • You influence through clarity, credibility and conviction rather than positional authority.
  • You understand that great strategy only matters if the field can execute it consistently.
  • You are a confident spokesperson who can represent CoreWeave’s Enterprise narrative in executive meetings, on stage and with the media.
  • You are motivated by building a category and changing how Enterprises think about AI infrastructure, not simply competing for individual transactions.

Why CoreWeave?

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun and move fast. We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth, we’re not afraid of a little chaos and we’re constantly learning.

Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

  • Be Curious at Your Core
  • Act Like an Owner
  • Empower Employees
  • Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences
  • Achieve More Together

We support an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking, and foster an environment that encourages collaboration and innovative solutions to complex problems. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, with the opportunity to help shape CoreWeave’s future.

Compensation

The starting salary will be determined by job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility).

About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Location: Our office is located in Oxford, England (UK), with hybrid working 
Job ID: 1820

The Role: 

We are looking for a Senior Electronics Engineer to join our Reliability Engineering team at IonQ. In this role, you will be responsible for finding, root-causing, and permanently resolving electronics  and control hardware issues on our operational trapped-ion quantum computers, contributing to the team's mission of improving fleet uptime and driving down the operational cost of our commercial and development systems.

You'll play an important part in owning the full lifecycle of electrical reliability fixes — from identifying a real-world bottleneck through to standardizing the resulting fix into every future build — working closely with Operations, Science, Manufacturing, and Engineering to keep our quantum systems running reliably and effectively. 

Responsibilities:

In this position, you will work on root-causing, designing, and deploying electronics system design fixes across our fleet of quantum systems, supporting the effective delivery of reliable, development and production hardware. You'll have the opportunity to drive system upgrades, standardize control and drive electronics across systems, and build the observability that catches problems before they cause downtime, contributing directly to the success of the Reliability Engineering team.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Triage & root cause: Actively monitor, root-cause, and prioritize electrical, control-system, and drive-electronics issues on live systems based on severity and impact to uptime and performance.
  • Solution development: Design, prototype, build, and test electrical fixes — spanning schematic capture, PCB layout, and board- and system-level test — taking solutions from concept through to permanent integration.
  • Reliability upgrade leadership: Drive electrical workstreams for major fleet-wide upgrades (e.g. control-hardware consolidation, drive-electronics standardization, remote telemetry/monitoring for laser and system health) to reduce variance and downtime across systems.
  • Retrofitting & deployment: Coordinate directly with Operations and Science teams to schedule, deploy, and retrofit upgrades onto live systems while managing operational constraints, and verify fixes improve system performance, reliability or operability. 
  • Documentation & standardization: Feed validated fixes back into engineering documentation, build manifests, and the Engineering Change Request (ECR) process so every improvement is baked into the baseline for all future builds.

Requirements:

To be successful, you will need strong foundations in analogue, RF, and mixed-signal electronics design, experience with the Altium PCB toolset, familiarity with RF concepts and confidence working directly on operational hardware under time pressure. We're looking for someone who can translate a system-level reliability problem into a concrete engineering solution, work across Operations, Science, and Engineering to get it deployed safely, and document it so it sticks. You'd be a great fit with:

  • Analogue and mixed-signal electronics: strong practical experience designing and debugging op-amp circuits, low-noise amplifiers, filters, ADC/DAC modules, grounding, shielding and common digital interfaces. 
  • Altium design control and documentation: strong experience managing evolving schematics and PCB designs in Altium, producing clear technical documentation, and establishing effective review, ERC/DRC, release and change-control processes. 
  • Fault-finding and electrical integration: able to diagnose power supplies, analogue circuits and control electronics, and develop reliable PCBs, adapters, connectors, breakout cables and harnesses. 
  • Stakeholder engagement and delivery: able to gather requirements, explain technical issues and trade-offs across different disciplines, and take solutions through testing, deployment and documentation. 
  • Bonus: familiarity with LVDS and FPGA-based control electronics, cryogenic or RF/microwave systems, and Python-based test automation or telemetry.

Vendor and supply

We are pioneering advancements in quantum computing by utilizing trapped ion technology and our proprietary laser-free quantum control methods. Our research and development efforts build on our fully integrated quantum processors that can be fabricated within standard silicon foundries. This unique approach allows us to leverage the highest-performing qubit technology while ensuring scalability and manufacturability using existing semiconductor fabrication technology. We approach quantum computing with a focus on minimizing errors, striving to achieve ultra-low gate errors at scale. Our immediate objective is to develop functional quantum computers within the NISQ regime, aiming to construct fault-tolerant machines that require minimal QEC overhead. Our recent breakthroughs include achieving 99.97% fidelity in two-qubit gates and 99.9992% fidelity in single-qubit operations without error correction, setting new industry standards for performance.

We are looking for Quantum Physicist to join our UK Science team at IonQ. Our Quantum Scientists work at the forefront of our research efforts to develop the next generation of quantum computers. 

They are responsible for validating and optimising the performance of our computers, playing a critical role in ensuring we are able to meet our research and development goals and timelines. Our Scientists’ work spans a broad range of areas from designing, coding, debugging and executing experiments, to developing and validating novel control schemes. They are responsible for documenting and sharing their findings with the aim of pushing the boundaries of system performance.

 

Responsibilities:

As a Senior Quantum Scientist, you will typically be responsible for a combination of these different responsibilities:

  • Prototyping and characterising coherent control and cooling schemes for trapped-ion qubits using laser and microwave fields.
  • Calibrating and benchmarking quantum systems, focusing on achieving the highest fidelities for quantum circuit primitives (e.g. ion transport or gate operations) and full circuits.
  • Validating emerging trap technologies, including integrated electronics and photonics for large-scale architectures.
  • Analysing experimental data, debug complex hardware/software interactions, and ensure reliability of qubit operations.

We’re looking for motivated scientists who can contribute to the progress of this fast moving, highly technical team and help the organisation meet our research goals.

  • Proven expertise in experimental AMO physics or quantum computing. Experience with trapped ions is beneficial though not essential.
  • Prior experience in one or more of the following: spectroscopy or coherent control of multi-level systems, characterisation of control hardware, gate fidelity benchmarking or running quantum circuits on hardware.
  • Strong proficiency in programming and data analysis, experience of Python or Rust is desirable.
  • Strong collaborative skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a fast-moving team.
  • A track record of scientific communication through publications, talks and conferences would be advantageous.

Be part of a team that’s shaping the future of quantum. We offer more than just a role, you’ll join a world class community of scientists, engineers and innovators working to unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

description:
Teamwork makes the stream work.

 

Roku is changing how the world watches TV

Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.

From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

 

 

What does the team work on?


At Roku, the Device Monetization and Themed Experiences (DMTE) team, a part of the Advertising organization, is where the magic behind the scenes happens. We're the engineers who build the high-performance graphics and UI foundations that power the AD Display — the core technology enabling Roku's smooth, responsive, and visually rich experiences on millions of devices worldwide. Our work lives in the middleware and UI layers, and its impact is felt every time a user navigates a menu, enjoys an animated ad, or is wowed by the bespoke experience built to market the latest TV show or Movies. We thrive on solving the toughest technical challenges — from optimizing UI rendering to fine-tuning memory usage — using BrightScript (a JavaScript-like language) to deliver rock-solid, high-performance solutions. We work in a collaborative, high-trust environment where great ideas can come from anywhere, partnering closely with firmware, UI, and product teams to ensure our platform is lightning fast, reliable, and ready for the next generation of streaming innovation. If you love building the invisible foundations that make great user experiences possible, this is the team for you.

 


What is the role?


As a Senior Agentic AI Engineer in the DMTE team, you'll be the driving force behind embedding intelligent, autonomous AI capabilities into Roku's platform — reimagining how our systems create, optimize, and deliver experiences to tens of millions of devices. Rather than building UI features directly, you'll design and deploy agentic AI systems that reason, plan, and act across our development and delivery pipelines — from automating the generation of themed experiences to enabling self-optimizing rendering workflows within the AD Display. You'll leverage your years of experience in software engineering and building world class UI to build AI agents that understand the constraints of embedded, performance-critical systems and operate effectively within them. This is a role for engineers who think in terms of autonomous systems, multi-step reasoning, and tool-use architectures — and who want to fundamentally reshape how a streaming platform is built, maintained, and evolved.

 

How will I use AI at Roku?

At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact. 
We value your AI skills if have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. And you can describe projects where you shipped real work with these tools. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.

 


What are the responsibilities of the role?

  • Apply strong software engineering principles to design, build, and ship reliable, performant systems at scale
  • Bring rigorous software engineering practices — clean architecture, testing, code review - to building systems that are reliable and performant at scale
  • Apply sound software engineering fundamentals (system design, testing, code review) to ship reliable, performant systems at scale
  • We don't train models, we don't 'fine-tune' LLMs; We build automated agentic processes
  • Design, build, and deploy agentic AI systems that autonomously generate, test, and optimize BrightScript/TypeScript code and UI experiences for the FRAME engine
  • Architect multi-agent workflows (planning, tool-use, retrieval, execution, validation) that accelerate development and reduce manual engineering effort across the team
  • Develop AI-powered automation that understands the constraints of embedded C++ environments and produces performance-safe, memory-efficient outputs
  • Build and maintain evaluation frameworks to measure agent reliability, accuracy, and performance in production-critical contexts
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (firmware, UI, product) to identify high-impact opportunities for AI-driven automation and intelligent tooling
  • Stay at the forefront of agentic AI research — including LLM orchestration, RAG, function calling, and autonomous code generation — and bring those advances into our platform
  • Mentor engineers across the team on AI-first development practices and help establish best practices for human-agent collaboration

 

What experience would help someone be successful in the role at Roku? 

  • Proven experience building agentic AI systems that generate, optimize, and deliver scalable applications in production environments
  • Strong software engineering foundation with a track record of shipping reliable, performant systems at scale
  • Deep familiarity with modern LLM orchestration tools, prompt engineering techniques, and AI/ML frameworks
  • Experience with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), function/tool calling, and evaluation-driven development for AI agents
  • A builder's mentality — you don't just use AI tools, you create autonomous systems that multiply the impact of entire teams
  • Proficiency in TypeScript (or similar languages) and Python for agent development, scripting, and pipeline automation
  • A software engineer's instinct for reliability, testability, and clean architecture — applied to the unique challenges of non-deterministic AI systems
  • Excellent technical communication, root cause analysis abilities, and a proactive mindset with passion for fast iteration

What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?

Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.

 

What are some of the benefits?

Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter.

 

Accommodations

Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to  

What should I know about Roku's culture?

Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV.

We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002.

About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Location: Oxford, UK
Office commitment: Hybrid

The Role:

Quantum is now, and it's built here. Oxford Ionics, now part of IonQ, is pioneering the next generation of quantum computing. Using our world-leading trapped-ion technology, we're building the most powerful, accurate and reliable quantum systems to tackle problems that today's supercomputers cannot solve.

We're looking for an enthusiastic and highly technical Senior Software Engineer for our non-realtime controllers team who will thrive in our dynamic cross-disciplinary environment. You will be working closely with our skilled software engineers, our systems teams who operate the physical quantum computers, and our world-leading quantum scientists to build and operate the software that controls the hardware surrounding our quantum computers. Previous exposure to quantum systems is not required.

You will own areas of the hardware control surface end to end, from the device protocol up to a service running reliably across our fleet. This is a hands-on engineering role and stays that way as you grow.

A working quantum computer is far more than the ion trap and its real-time control electronics. It depends on a fleet of supporting hardware, including cryogenic compressors, vacuum pumps, power supplies, lasers, temperature controllers, wavemeters and cameras, that has to be kept observable, controllable and reliable. The timing-critical operations such as gate waveforms and ion transport run on dedicated real-time FPGA systems, while this team owns everything that does not need hard timing guarantees. These services run on general-purpose Linux hardware and must be rock-solid, because a failed compressor or an un-noticed pressure drift takes a whole machine offline.

Responsibilities:

This is a hands-on engineering role, balancing delivery of your own areas with support for the teams and scientists who depend on them.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Own a group of device controllers end to end, covering API design, implementation, rollout and ongoing operational health.
  • Make services robust against the ways real instruments fail.
  • Bring devices onto our current framework, and roll the result out across the fleet without disrupting running experiments.
  • Improve the shared framework where a problem turns out to be common to many controllers rather than specific to one.
  • Work closely with the systems teams and scientists who depend on these services, and strengthen observability, health checking and alerting.
  • Raise the standard of the code around you through review, and bring less experienced engineers on by working alongside them.

Requirements:

To be successful, you will need experience working with Linux based systems and interfacing with hardware, and a track record of making software behave well against unreliable external dependencies. We're looking for someone who can own a problem area with little supervision and judge where robustness is worth the effort.

You’d be a great fit with:

  • Strong systems engineering skills. Our controllers are written in Rust, so either solid Rust experience or deep proficiency in another systems language and the appetite to work in a Rust codebase, including async programming.
  • Experience designing and operating networked services such as gRPC or REST, with a real grasp of error handling, observability and failure modes.
  • Experience of hardware and instrument protocols and interfaces such as SCPI, Modbus, serial and Ethernet.
  • Comfortable owning the production behaviour of what you build, not just its correctness in test.
  • Excellent communication skills both within software and across disciplines, and an interest in helping other engineers get better at the craft without wanting to stop building yourself.

Benefits

Be part of a team that’s shaping the future of quantum. We offer more than just a role, you’ll join a world class community of scientists, engineers and innovators working to unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

We offer a range of benefits, including opportunities to further your career alongside industry leaders, a competitive salary with IonQ stock options, an annual performance bonus, generous annual leave, flexible hybrid working, private medical and dental insurance for you and your family, and much more.

Join us and be part of the future of quantum computing.

Role:

 

We are looking for a Staff Analog Mixed-Signal Design and Verification Engineer to join our Cryo-CMOS IC team at IonQ Oxford. In this role, you will design analog and mixed-signal blocks from specification through circuit design, simulation, layout, tape-out and silicon validation. You will also own top-level chip integration and modelling as a first-class part of our Cryo-CMOS development flow. In this you will build and maintain the model of the chip that the whole team simulates against, a mixed-abstraction model combining transistor-level circuits with Verilog-A/Verilog-AMS and SystemVerilog real-number behavioural blocks. You will decide which blocks are represented at which level of abstraction, keep the models faithful to the schematics and measured silicon. The full-chip model will then be used to verify the ASICs that control the quantum processor from room temperature down to a few kelvin.

You'll play an important part in shaping the design, modelling and verification methodology, standards and sign-off criteria that support our work in building the world's most advanced quantum systems.

 

Responsibilities:

 

In this position, you will build and maintain the model of the chip that the whole team simulates against, a mixed-abstraction model combining transistor-level circuits with Verilog-A/Verilog-AMS and SystemVerilog real-number behavioural blocks. These models will be derived form first-principles mathematics and correlated against schematic and measured silicon. You will decide which blocks are represented at which level of abstraction, keep the models faithful to the schematics and measured silicon. The full-chip model will then be used to verify the ASICs that control the quantum processor from room temperature down to a few kelvin.

You'll have the opportunity to set the design and modelling standards the programme signs off against, making trusted models to inform tape-out decisions, and raise the design and modelling capability of the engineers around you, contributing directly to the success of IonQ's quantum computing roadmap.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Own the full-chip modelling strategy: model architecture, abstraction levels, accuracy targets and sign-off criteria used across the IC development flow
  • Owning analog and mixed-signal blocks (references, DACs, switches, regulators, clock distribution) from specification through schematic design
  • Own top-level integration: define block interfaces and specifications, assemble the top level, and run the full-chip mixed-signal simulations that verify the ASIC Develop Verilog-A and Verilog-AMS models of analog blocks and assemble them into a simulatable full chip
  • Build real-number models so the full chip runs in digital verification and regression at practical speed
  • Derive models from mathematics: turn a transfer function, a Z-parameter network description or a MATLAB analysis into robust Verilog-A with well-behaved tolerances
  • Define and run model-versus-schematic correlation, keeping models in sync with design releases, and feed measured silicon behaviour, back into the models and the block designs
  • Stand up mixed-signal co-simulation and regression (Cadence AMS Designer, Xcelium with Spectre) Lead block-level design reviews and mentor engineers on circuit design and modelling craft

Requirements:

To be successful, you will need deep analog and mixed-signal design and modelling experience, typically 10+ years. You will have designed blocks proven in silicon and models and used in production tape-out flows. You will bring expert transistor-level design of precision analog blocks (references, DACs, regulators, switches, clock distribution) taken through PVT and Monte Carlo, layout and silicon validation, together with expert Verilog-A and Verilog-AMS and strong real-number modelling.

You’d be a great fit with:

  • Multiple tape-outs with responsibility for block design and top-level integration, including silicon bring-up and bench characterisation
  • Strong mathematical foundations: linear systems, Laplace and z-domain analysis, network (Z-) parameters, noise and non-linearity
  • Fluency in a production Cadence flow: Virtuoso, Spectre, Xcelium and AMS Designer or similar co-simulation environments, including parasitic extraction and post-layout sign-off
  • SystemVerilog, plus MATLAB or Python/NumPy for analysis and model validation; scripting to automate model generation, checking and regression
  • Cryogenic, space or other extreme-environment silicon experience will be highly beneficial, especially designing beyond foundry model validity using measured device data

We're looking for someone who can design a block to specification and model it at the right fidelity, derive a model from equations and implement it end to end. You should be able to judge what to model and at what abstraction, align designers, verification and systems engineers on what a model does and does not promise, and contribute effectively within a fast-moving, highly technical team.

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Location: Oxford, UK
Job ID:  1831

The Role: 

We are looking for a Systems Software Engineer to join our Runtime Software team at Oxford Ionics / IonQ. In this role, you will be responsible for working directly with the experimental scientists to implement the real-time control system behaviours and provide abstractions they require for their experiments, contributing to the team’s mission of enabling our science teams to experiment and improve the primitive operations which allow compute, and building towards fault tolerant computation.

You’ll play an important part in shaping the core, Rust, libraries and the execution environment which take our system from a collection of hardware to a quantum computer, and support our work in building the world’s most advanced quantum systems.

 

Responsibilities:

In this position, you will work on developing abstractions over real-time control hardware, supporting the effective delivery of a control system capable of repeatedly and reproducibly driving our ions with nano-second level precision, with abstractions which are conducive to both fast iteration and system scaling.

You’ll have the opportunity to accelerate the science core to the development of our systems, and contribute to the core execution model of our quantum computers, contributing directly to the success of building utility-scale quantum computers.

Key responsibilities include: 

  • Collaborating with scientists to understand their requirements.
  • Interfacing with system orchestration, non-realtime control and compiler teams to ensure our work integrates seamlessly with the wider software architecture.
  • Implementing drivers for various real-time devices.
  • Producing tooling to enable users of our code to iterate rapidly and fearlessly.
  • Developing the execution environment for the user programs which run on our systems.
  • Continually improving the APIs used by our internal users.

 

Requirements:

To be successful, you will need expert programming skills in a systems programming language and a desire to produce high quality code appropriate to a real-time environment. We’re looking for someone who can quickly iterate on low-level code in a collaborative, cross-disciplinary, environment and contribute effectively within a fast moving, highly technical team.

You’d be a great fit if you:

  • Have strong programming skills in one or more mainstream programming languages
  • Have experience with a systems programming programming
  • Have an interest in or experience with Rust
  • Have developed excellent communication skills both within the context of software and across disciplines
  • Are comfortable working with rapidly evolving requirements
  • Are used to maintaining and producing high quality code reviews and appropriate testing
  • Have a desire to maximize impact through quick iteration and short cycles of learning and improvement
  • Are eager to learn and develop your skills

About Nscale

Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud supports strategic business outcomes including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you’ll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work.

About the Role

We are looking for a Principal Presales Engineer / Solutions Architect to join Nscale’s commercial organisation and play a key role in helping customers understand, evaluate, and adopt our AI infrastructure solutions.

This is a deeply technical, customer-facing role at the intersection of sales, solution design, and AI infrastructure. You will partner closely with account executives, product, engineering, and operations teams to support the full sales cycle, from discovery and technical qualification through solution design, product demonstrations, proof of concept support, and customer onboarding.

You will need to quickly become fluent in Nscale’s infrastructure, platform capabilities, and software orchestration stack so that you can confidently present our solutions, map customer requirements to technical architectures, and act as a trusted advisor throughout the buying journey.

This role is ideal for someone who combines strong technical credibility with commercial instinct, enjoys engaging directly with customers, and can translate complex GPU, AI, and cloud concepts into clear business value.

What You’ll Do

  • Support the commercial team in qualifying customer opportunities and identifying technical requirements early in the sales process
  • Deliver compelling product demos, technical presentations, workshops, and architecture sessions for prospective customers and partners
  • Translate customer AI, HPC, and infrastructure requirements into clear solution designs using Nscale’s platform
  • Develop and present solution proposals that align technical architecture with customer business outcomes
  • Work closely with customers to understand workloads, deployment requirements, performance expectations, and scaling plans
  • Build a strong working knowledge of Nscale’s infrastructure stack, GPU cloud platform, APIs, orchestration tooling, and deployment models
  • Support proof of concepts, evaluations, onboarding projects, and technical validation activities
  • Partner with product, engineering, and operations teams to ensure proposed solutions are realistic, scalable, and aligned with platform standards
  • Provide guidance on compute, networking, storage, orchestration, and workload optimisation for AI and machine learning use cases
  • Help create repeatable demo environments, technical playbooks, reference architectures, and sales enablement materials
  • Act as a technical voice in the commercial organisation, helping shape how Nscale positions its solutions in the market
  • Surface customer feedback, product gaps, and recurring technical objections to internal stakeholders
  • Support RFQ, BOM, and technical proposal development where required for larger or more complex opportunities

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience in presales engineering, solutions architecture, sales engineering, cloud architecture, or a similar customer-facing technical role
  • Strong ability to present technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Experience supporting enterprise or mid-market sales cycles in infrastructure, cloud, AI, data centre, or platform environments
  • Good understanding of cloud infrastructure, GPU compute, AI/ML workloads, or high-performance infrastructure
  • Familiarity with containers, Kubernetes, Slurm, orchestration platforms, or workload deployment models
  • Understanding of networking, storage, and distributed compute concepts in modern infrastructure environments
  • Ability to quickly learn a complex technical platform and confidently represent it externally
  • Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work cross-functionally across sales, engineering, product, and operations
  • Commercial awareness and the ability to link technical solution design to customer outcomes and deal progression
  • Strong written skills for creating solution overviews, proposals, diagrams, and customer-facing technical content

Nice to Have

  • Terraform or related orchestration and automation tools
  • Experience delivering technical product demos in a presales or partner-facing environment
  • Experience supporting AI start-ups, research organisations, model builders, or enterprise AI teams
  • Understanding of high-performance networking concepts such as InfiniBand, RDMA, or RoCE
  • Experience working with APIs, developer platforms, or cloud-native application environments
  • Experience with open-weight model training and inference

What Success Looks Like

  • You can confidently demo Nscale’s platform and explain its value to both technical and commercial stakeholders
  • You become a trusted technical partner to the sales team and help accelerate qualified opportunities
  • You can quickly assess customer requirements and map them to practical, compelling solution designs and architectures
  • You help improve win rates by addressing technical objections with clarity and credibility
  • You contribute to a repeatable presales motion through strong documentation, demos, and enablement content
  • You build deep knowledge of Nscale’s infrastructure and software orchestration capabilities and use that knowledge to support customer adoption

Why Join Nscale

At Nscale, you’ll help shape how customers adopt next-generation AI infrastructure. You’ll work with fast-growing AI companies and enterprise organisations, support strategic customer engagements, and play a visible role in translating Nscale’s technical capabilities into commercial success.

You’ll be joining a company at the forefront of GPU cloud infrastructure, with the opportunity to influence customer outcomes, product feedback loops, and go-to-market execution. This role offers the chance to combine technical depth with real commercial impact.

Inclusion at Nscale

At Nscale, we are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives enriches our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities.

We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, careers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

The Role:

Quantum is now, and it's built here. Oxford Ionics, now part of IonQ, is pioneering the next generation of quantum computing. Using our world-leading trapped-ion technology, we're building the most powerful, accurate and reliable quantum systems to tackle problems that today's supercomputers cannot solve.

We're looking for an enthusiastic and highly technical Staff Software Engineer for our non-realtime controllers team who will thrive in our dynamic cross-disciplinary environment. You'd be working closely with our skilled software engineers, our systems teams who operate the physical quantum computers, and our world-leading quantum scientists to build and operate the software that controls the hardware surrounding our quantum computers. Previous exposure to quantum systems is not required.

You will take on our most demanding hardware integrations and the framework work that makes every other controller better. This is a hands-on engineering role: you would be the most experienced engineer writing controllers, not the one directing others to write them.

A working quantum computer is far more than the ion trap and its real-time control electronics. It depends on a fleet of supporting hardware, including cryogenic compressors, vacuum pumps, power supplies, lasers, temperature controllers, wavemeters and cameras, that has to be kept observable, controllable and reliable. The timing-critical operations such as gate waveforms and ion transport run on dedicated real-time FPGA systems, while this team owns everything that does not need hard timing guarantees. These services run on general-purpose Linux hardware and must be rock-solid, because a failed compressor or an un-noticed pressure drift takes a whole machine offline.

This is a hands-on engineering role. Your influence comes from the code you ship and review, and from the problems you take off everyone else's plate.

  • Take on our most demanding device integrations, and do the deep diagnosis of problems that only appear against real hardware in a live lab.

  • Experience of hardware and instrument protocols and interfaces such as SCPI, Modbus, serial and Ethernet.

  • Excellent communication skills both within software and across disciplines.
